row_data.body: Paint is wrapped up on my unit - walls and trim all done, moved this one to In Progress. Plumbing repair is next on my list before we can call it ready for inspection.

Looked through Carlos's update on the water heater findings - those replacements are going to hit the budget harder than the other plumbing items, so I want to flag that as something we need to account for as we move forward. I've cross-posted the cost concern to #budget-review so the right people have eyes on it. Teresa is putting a mid-initiative check-in on the calendar for the first week of June so we can regroup on overall progress before the push wraps up.

Just added Linda Castillo's mid-year review to the calendar for mid-June - Teresa has it scheduled. One thing to flag for whoever is pulling her packet together: Linda consistently zeroes in on tenant retention, so make sure the materials lead with lease renewal rates and a breakdown of any move-out reasons from the first half of the year.

Carlos confirmed in #maintenance that access notices are out for the first wave of South cluster units. Moving this to In Progress - here's how the week shakes out: Units 102, 105, and 108 are scheduled for Monday, 103 and 107 on Wednesday, and 101 and 106 wrapping up Friday. Windows run 9 a.m. to noon each day per the approved entries Carlos shared.

Moving this up to In Review - all four owner meetings are confirmed on the calendar, each review packet is put together, and everything is staged for Aurora to give a final look before we sit down with Robert Finley. Good work from everyone on pulling this together.

Wrapped up the May 30 review with Robert - he's happy with where occupancy and collections landed, acknowledged the maintenance pass-throughs without issue, and asked us to keep him updated on the vacant unit's re-lease status by mid-June. Moving this to In Review now that the meeting is fully closed out.

Ran spot-checks on a sample from both the South and North clusters this afternoon - airflow, coil condition, and refrigerant levels all came back clean across every unit I pulled. No issues to flag on either side, so I'm moving both cluster issues to Done. Good work from Elias, Wesley, Carlos, and Tony getting everything buttoned up cleanly.

Splitting the prep between Lisa and Patricia to keep things manageable - Lisa, you've got Harry Harris and Robert Finley; Patricia, you've got David Shea and Linda Castillo. I need occupancy rates, outstanding maintenance backlog, and make-ready status for each of your owners pulled together no later than the second week of May. Dropping a note in the general PM channel now so everyone has the same deadline in front of them.

Before Tuesday's review meeting, I want to propose we address the overage by reallocating the deferred preventive-maintenance line items from the Preventive Maintenance Push budget into the Make-Ready overage to offset what's already been spent. On top of that, I think we have enough summer turns remaining across the portfolio to go back to the carpet vendor and negotiate a volume discount - if we bundle the remaining units, we should have real leverage. Dave, Lisa, and Patricia, can you each confirm how many carpet turns you still have scheduled through end of August so I can put together a consolidated ask before I reach out to them?

Wesley and I finished out the remaining North cluster units this afternoon - he jumped in to help push through the last few and we got everything covered. Moving this to In Review now that the full North cluster is wrapped.
Went through each East cluster unit and left final notes on the issue - coil cleaning and A/C checks are all wrapped up across the board. Moving this to In Review for Jaime to look over.

South cluster is fully wrapped - every unit got serviced this week, so I'm moving this to In Review for Brooke to look over. Tony, noted on the North side; Carlos, can you get a second round of access notices out to those two remaining tenants so we can get them on the books before the push closes out?

Good news on Mesa Vista - Lisa confirmed the make-ready turn is finishing up this week, and the leasing team is already lining up showings for next week. That wraps up Robert's last open question from the May report review, so I'm moving this to Done. All follow-up items are closed out.

Moving this to In Progress - started working through the battery replacements this morning. Units 101, 102, and 103 are done, detectors tested and good. Unit 104 needed a second battery (both slots were dead), swapped out and confirmed working. Finishing up the remaining units now and will update once the full property is cleared.

Wrapping up on this one - the full case file for the Mitchell hearing is assembled and organized, and Harry has everything he needs going in. Based on what Patricia Lowe indicated about the JP court's current docket, we're in a solid position and expect a favorable ruling. Closing this out as ready; I'll reopen if anything comes up after the hearing.
Paint is wrapped up on my unit - walls and trim look good, ready for the next trade. Still waiting on the plumber to confirm his slot before I can move that one forward.

Wrapped up the first pass on the North Cluster units this morning. Condenser coils are showing moderate fouling across the board - nothing catastrophic, but a couple of units are bad enough that I'd call them immediate rather than routine. Plumbing fixtures have the usual wear you'd expect at this age: a few slow drains and one bathroom faucet with a noticeably worn cartridge. Electrical panels looked okay overall, no obvious hazards, though one unit had a double-tapped breaker worth flagging for the electrician. Heads-up that I also dropped a summary in #make-ready - two units need HVAC attention before anything else moves forward on them.

Going with the brand-compliant vendor on this one, Carlos - want to keep our signage consistent across the portfolio. Charge it to the marketing and signage line in the operating budget. Moving this to In Review so we can get eyes on it before we finalize the order.

Just got word from Carlos that this unit has a confirmed move-in in early June, so I'm bumping this to Urgent and moving it to the front of the queue - we need to have it rent-ready well before that date. Let's make sure paint, flooring, appliances, and the deep clean are all sequenced this week so there's no last-minute scramble. - Brooke

Drafted the full narrative for Robert's May report - occupancy section runs unit by unit across Mesa Vista with the 94% figure and context on the one unit still vacant, rent collection notes the late payment from last month and confirms it's been resolved, maintenance summary covers all tickets opened and closed in May plus vendor dispatch costs with the water heater subfloor repair called out as a pass-through, make-ready section gives the current turnover status on the vacant unit with our projected rent-ready date heading into June, and I wrapped up with a short portfolio condition note flagging HVAC readiness as summer approaches. Moving this to In Progress - Lisa and Teresa, let me know if anything looks off before I send it to Robert.

Moving this to In Progress - Lisa has occupancy and maintenance data pulled for both Harris and Finley, and Patricia is working through her owner packages as well. Teresa has Robert Finley's portfolio review locked in for the first week of June, 60 minutes in the afternoon, and he wants the numbers sent over before the call so he can come prepared.

Heads up, Carlos - a few of the units at the upcoming property on my plate have occupied tenants, so I'll need to coordinate entry windows before we can get in to complete the filter replacements and detector checks. Can you help me line up confirmed access times with those residents so we don't show up unannounced or hit any scheduling conflicts?
Ran a spot-check across all units this morning - filters look good across the board, no issues flagged and nothing needs to go back for rework. Moving this to In Review.

Closing out the week - moving 114B to Done now that it cleared QC. For the weekly picture: one unit fully turned and leased-ready, 112A still in progress pending the cabinet hardware fix before it can close, and Lisa flagged two more vacancies coming off lease end of May that we'll need to slot into the Summer Make-Ready Program queue. Updated the overall program status on Linear to reflect where we landed heading into next week.

Logging decisions from today's sync: Elias, you're taking point on reaching out to the carpet vendor directly to get something on the schedule this week - let us know once you have a day confirmed. I've moved the target date on this issue to reflect the delay. Also worth noting for backlog planning - Lisa flagged that two more vacancies are coming at the end of May, so those units will be rolling into the make-ready queue once they turn.

Patricia, can you pull together the documentation package for the Mitchell case - we'll need the original lease, the full payment ledger, and all notice-to-vacate records on file. Once you have those compiled, I'll reach out to Harry Harris directly to walk him through the hearing details.

Wrapped up QC walks on both units the techs flagged as ready this morning. The first one cleared - everything looks good to move forward on that one. The second unit needs some punch-list work before it's done: cabinet hardware has to be addressed and there are a few spots that need touch-up paint. Documenting the rework items on that unit's issue now so Elias and the team can pick it up.
Went through each East cluster unit this afternoon and dropped final notes on the issue - coil cleaning and filter checks all done across the board. Moving this to In Review for Jaime to look over.

Synced up on next steps - Elias, you're owning outreach to the carpet vendor to lock in something this week. I've pushed the target date on this issue to reflect the updated timeline. Also flagging for the group: Lisa just noted in #make-ready that two more units are vacating at the end of May, so those will be coming into the backlog once we clear the current queue.

Quick question before I move forward - I've got quotes from two vendors for the exterior directional signage at Sunset Ridge, Las Palmas, and Mesa Vista. The lower-cost option comes in noticeably cheaper, but the second vendor's materials and font choices actually match our brand guidelines. Which direction do we want to go, Brooke? Happy to move fast once I have the call on this.

Logging Robert's follow-up questions from the May 30 review along with my answers for the record: he asked about the re-lease timeline and marketing plan for the vacant Mesa Vista unit, and I confirmed the leasing team is actively working it with showings already on the books. On the water heater flooring repair, that cost falls within the standard maintenance reserve - no separate capital allocation needed. For the Summer Make-Ready Program budget impact, I explained that the program costs are being offset by reduced vacancy loss and stronger tenant retention across the portfolio, so the net effect on his operating budget is favorable.

Ran spot-checks on a sample of units across both the South and North clusters this morning - airflow was solid throughout, coils came back clean, and refrigerant levels looked correct on every unit I pulled. Everything cleared QC, so I've moved both cluster issues to Done.

Wrapped up QC walks on both units this afternoon. The first one is good to go - everything looked clean and solid, marking it clear for leasing. The second one isn't quite there yet: cabinet hardware is missing a couple of pieces and there are some scuffs that need touch-up paint before it's ready. I'll drop the punch-list details on that unit's issue so Elias and the guys can knock it out.

Marking this Done - the approved reallocation figures are locked in and the June and July make-ready turns can move forward under the revised line items. Teresa has posted the confirmation in #budget-review, so everyone working those turns should have what they need. Thanks to the whole group for working through this quickly.

Wrapping up the South cluster runs for this week - most units went smoothly. One exception: the condensate drain on the unit at the end of my second building was badly clogged and needed an extended flush to clear fully, so that one took longer than planned. Also have one unit where the tenant wasn't home during the access window; I need to get a reschedule coordinated before I can close that one out. Tony, good to see North cluster moving - let me know if you hit anything similar on the drain lines over there.

Marking this one Done - great work pulling the checklist together and piloting it with maintenance, Lisa. We'll be rolling the updated form out across the full portfolio starting next week, so everyone should expect it to land in your workflows shortly.

Just heard from Patricia Lowe over at the JP court - she confirmed the hearing date is officially on the docket for the Mitchell case. I've opened this issue so we can keep tabs on where things stand and make sure Brooke and Teresa have what they need to stay ready as we move through the court process. Harry will need a heads-up once we have the full schedule nailed down.

All South cluster units are done - coil cleaning finished across every property in the batch, no outstanding items. Moving this to In Review for Brooke to look over. Tony, I saw your note on the North cluster issue; Carlos, go ahead and send that second round of access notices to the two remaining tenants so Tony can get those wrapped up before the mid-point check-in. - Elias

Finished running through all the units in my cluster today. Two water heaters are showing enough wear that I'd call them replacements rather than repairs - I'll flag those for Brooke to get vendor quotes lined up. Also found hose bibs at a few units that need attention before we head into summer heat; nothing urgent but definitely shouldn't sit. Moving this to In Progress now that I've got eyes on everything.

Paint is wrapped up on my unit - walls look solid, no touch-ups needed. Moving this one to In Progress. Plumbing repair is still on the list for the next unit; waiting to confirm the schedule with the vendor before I push that forward.

Preparation checklist is updated on this issue. Documents are pulled together and organized, witness availability has been confirmed with Harry, and I've flagged the remaining outstanding items we still need to close out before the hearing. Moving this to active preparation - let me know if anything on the checklist needs a second look, Brooke.

Drafted the updated move-out walkthrough checklist and ran it through an actual turnover at my site this week - it held up well and captured everything we typically miss across properties. Ready for the team to review whenever Brooke, Carlos, Patricia, and Teresa want to take a look before we roll it out portfolio-wide.

Wesley and I knocked out the remaining North cluster units this afternoon - he jumped in and we worked through them together to get it done. Marking this one In Review; Elias, East cluster is yours now, good luck out there.

South cluster update: most units are wrapped up. One unit had a clogged condensate drain that took extra flush time to clear - all good now, but worth noting for the service log. The other holdout is the unit where the tenant wasn't home during our window, so I need to get a reschedule on the books with Carlos to coordinate a new entry time. Tony, glad to see North cluster moving - let me know if you run into anything similar on the drain lines over there.
Closet-door hardware replaced and realigned — doors slide clean and latch properly. Closing.
Tightened the P-trap slip nut and swapped the worn washer; ran water for five minutes with no drip. Closing.

The 8D disposal is seized, not just jammed — the motor won't reset and the flywheel is frozen. This needs a full unit replacement, not a repair. Routing back to you for parts approval before I swap it. — James
Hill Country Plumbing replaced the pool pump motor and pressure switch on-site Tuesday; system pressure-tested and back online Wednesday afternoon. Pool reopened. Closing.
